newsitem.title: USA: Noteholders file to force Claridge bankruptcy.
newsitem.headline: Noteholders file to force Claridge bankruptcy.

text.p: Three noteholders on Wednesday filed a petition to force Claridge Hotel & Casino Corp into bankruptcy, according to noteholders counsel David Pikus.

The move comes less than one week after a committee of noteholders sued Claridge in an attempt to garner full redemption value of outstanding first mortgage notes. Claridge had indicated it would not make a scheduled February interest payment on the notes, sending the company into default.

The petition puts Claridge in a gap period, Pikus said. During that time, Claridge can operate, but can also have the advantage of an automatic stay, which could suspend any litigation or claims against the company, he said.

The lawsuit against Claridge will thus be stayed, Pikus said, but it remains active against the other defendants -- Oppenheimer & Co, a Claridge operating company and a Claridge real estate parnership.
The petition was filed in U.S. Bankruptcy court in Camden, New Jersey, Pikus said.

In addition to the Claridge default, the noteholders are also pursuing full payment of the notes should Hilton Hotels Corp follow through on a proposed acquisition of Claridge. Hilton has proposed buying back notes it does not already own at less than face value.
(( -- Al Yoon, U.S. Corporate Bond Desk, 212-859-1672 ))
